item.title: Nation's role in world auto sector on show
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
International automakers and suppliers are giving China a bigger role in their global businesses, using the country not only as a major market but as a base for developing vehicles, technologies and supply chains for overseas markets. The trend is evident at the ninth China International Import Expo, which opened in Shanghai on Thursday. Volkswagen Group is presenting seven vehicles from its Volkswagen, Audi and Porsche brands at the expo, four of which are new energy vehicles. The display comes as the German automaker seeks to make China an important source of innovation and products for markets beyond the country. Two models making their debut at the expo — the SAIC Volkswagen ID. ERA 5X SUV and FAW-Volkswagen ID. AURA L5 sedan — feature locally developed intelligent driving technology, while the ID. ERA 5X uses a 4-nanometer cockpit chip. The group says its broader China strategy is to develop technologies and vehicles domestically that can also serve other markets, particularly in the Global South. Within the group, Porsche is using the expo to highlight opportunities in China's automotive aftermarket as well as its established car business. Its exhibits include the 911 GT4 R supercar, which made its public debut in China, the China-exclusive Panamera Pure Edition sedan, and a classic 1961 Porsche 356 B 1600 S Roadster. The company is also working with Shanghai's Jiading district on classic-car activities, including vehicle displays and driving experiences. "We do not simply provide professional race cars. We also aim to create a progressive pathway for drivers, from their first experience on track to professional competition," said Alexandre Gibot, managing director of Porsche Motorsport Asia Pacific.

item.title: Translation earbuds break language barriers for tai chi learners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
When Jerome Lepeu from France steps onto the floor for his tai chi lesson in Beijing on a Saturday afternoon, he is learning more than a sequence of slow, flowing movements. Lepeu, 64, is also learning a new "language" — the terminology of tai chi — that can be difficult to grasp even when spoken in his mother tongue. Some of his instructor's explanations are abstract, as she describes how to direct force through the body, where to place one's weight and how to coordinate movement with breathing. For a foreign student unfamiliar with the terminology, understanding what lies behind each gesture can be as challenging as performing it. But Lepeu has found an unexpected aid: a pair of translation earbuds. He began studying tai chi about a year ago, and his instructor, Wang Jingyun, provided him with the earbuds to help him follow her lessons. As Wang explains the principles behind a movement in Chinese, the earbuds translate her words into a language he understands, allowing him to focus on both the physical movements and their underlying meaning. "Many of the descriptions in tai chi are quite abstract. It's not always easy to understand what the teacher means just by watching the movements," Lepeu said. "With the translation earbuds, I can understand how to apply force and what each movement is actually about." For him, the technology has made a noticeable difference. Instead of relying solely on imitation, he can better understand the reasoning behind the movements, an important part of learning an art form whose physical techniques and philosophical ideas are closely intertwined. Wang, who has more than 30 years of experience studying and teaching tai chi, has also noticed how translation technology is changing the way she works with international students. She has taught a number of learners from overseas, many of whom use translation earbuds to follow her instructions. The devices have made communication more efficient, helping students grasp explanations that might otherwise require repeated demonstrations or lengthy attempts to clarify through gestures. "Tai chi involves a lot of explanations about how the body moves and how force is generated. Some concepts are difficult to convey through movements alone," Wang said. "With the earbuds, students can understand what I'm saying more directly, which makes teaching and learning much easier." The experience in Wang's classroom reflects a growing overseas market for AI-powered translation earbuds, many of which are developed and sold by Chinese startups. On TikTok, short videos promoting the devices have attracted attention by highlighting familiar situations in which language barriers can cause awkwardness or inconvenience. In one popular advertising scenario, a customer in the United States visits a nail salon where the technician is a Vietnamese immigrant. Wearing translation earbuds, the customer can finally follow the technician's conversation. Other videos show taxi drivers using the devices to communicate with passengers from different countries. For Chinese entrepreneurs, the appeal lies partly in combining relatively affordable hardware with increasingly accessible AI translation services. Rather than carrying a separate translation device or repeatedly checking a smartphone, users can wear the earbuds and communicate more naturally while going about daily activities. "We're only at the beginning of this market," said Zhang Zejie, founder of Shanghai-based NebulaBuds, an AI-powered software platform that enables ordinary Bluetooth earbuds to offer real-time translation and other intelligent features. This has helped Chinese manufacturers tap into growing overseas demand for AI audio devices. Zhang said the global translation earbud market currently ships around 1.5 million units a month, adding that it still has considerable room to expand, potentially growing fivefold to tenfold. "Translation earbuds can remain relevant over the next five to 10 years, with their portability, improving technology and growing demand for cross-cultural communication," he said. "As more people travel, study and work overseas, the need to communicate across language barriers will continue to grow, creating new opportunities for the industry." Translation earbuds are designed primarily for everyday conversations, such as ordering food, asking for directions, taking taxis or shopping, making them potentially useful for tourists traveling abroad or foreign visitors in China. "However, the technology still has limitations. Background noise, accents, rapid speech and overlapping conversations can affect accuracy, while idioms and specialized terminology remain difficult to translate reliably," Zhang said. "Improving translation accuracy and making conversations more natural are still important areas of development," he added.

item.title: Airborne wind power system aces trial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
The world's first 4,000-meter-class airborne wind power generation system successfully completed its test flight recently in Yueyang, Hunan province. The launch marked the system's first trial in an urban scenario, proving its future potential to harness wind power and supply it to densely populated areas to meet people's power demands. Measuring 67 meters long, 40 meters wide and 23 meters high, with a maximum ascent altitude of 4,000 meters, the system delivers output voltage ranging from 10 to 35 kilovolts and boasts a designed service life of 20 years, according to the developer, Beijing SAWES TO ONE Technology. Named the Stratosphere Airborne Wind Energy System, it uses a helium-filled airborne platform to carry lightweight power generation modules several kilometers aloft. It harnesses steady high-altitude winds for continuous power generation, and the electricity produced is transmitted back to the ground via tether cables. "The urban test flight assesses whether the system can operate safely and reliably when flown near residents and crowds. Cities are core power consumption areas, and ultimately, we aim to deploy this power supply system in more densely populated regions," said Dun Tianrui, founder and CEO of the company. The Yueyang launch involved multidimensional verification tests, including attitude stability control under complex airflow and performance testing in complex magnetic field environments. High-altitude wind energy, an untapped frontier of new energy yet to be developed on a large scale, boasts advantages such as higher wind speeds, steady wind directions and high wind energy density. It occupies no land space and can reduce grid construction costs of ultra-high voltage transmission channels for new energy, Dun said. The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) for renewable energy development outlined how research will be carried out on efficient and reliable wind power generation equipment technologies to achieve breakthroughs in manufacturing technologies for key equipment such as highly reliable, low-cost blades, ultra-high towers and innovative floating foundations, and to explore high-altitude wind power and other new wind energy utilization technologies. "Instead of merely serving unmanned zones and other power supply scenarios, the system is designed for direct integration into the main power grid in cities," Dun said. Relying on its self-power generation capacity and easy deployment, the system can also deliver clean power to areas with limited power access and high electricity costs, such as remote mountainous regions, islands, mining areas and industrial parks. The company will continue to upgrade and iterate its performance to tap wind energy resources at higher altitudes, according to Dun. Cai Rong, a researcher at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences, told China Central Television News that the test flight in an urban scenario mainly aims to verify the reliability of the complete airborne system. It also assesses the feasibility and integrity of engineering delivery under real-world operating conditions around cities, as well as the capability for rapid on-site deployment. The test gave strong impetus to the transition of high-altitude wind power equipment from technical validation to industrial application, he said. The system also drew widespread admiration from foreign guests attending the third China-Africa Energy Cooperation Project Promotion Conference in Yueyang earlier this month. "This city can use technology and AI to produce cheap electricity and energy for the people here. As an African country, we trust the Chinese enterprises, so they are welcome to come to our country," said Abubaker Bensaud, a Libyan embassy representative in China. item.title: CPC's practice in governance inspires world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
Over the course of some 17 visits to China, Morris Tovebae, general secretary of Papua New Guinea's ruling Pangu Party, has witnessed the country's remarkable transformation and sought to understand what lies behind its success. Tovebae said that the changes he saw prompted him to ask himself, "What's the magic?" Through his repeated visits, he gradually found an answer in the Communist Party of China's strong leadership and organizational system, Tovebae said in an interview with China Daily. What particularly impressed him was the CPC's extensive grassroots network, which he said helps connect government decisions with people's needs and development priorities. Inspired by what he has seen, Tovebae is seeking to strengthen his own party by drawing on the CPC's organizational experience. He is particularly interested in China's Party school system and hopes to establish a similar institution in Papua New Guinea to train party members and political leaders, helping the Pangu Party build lasting organizational strength. However, maintaining that organizational strength presents a continuing challenge for the CPC: how to sustain effective leadership and discipline across its vast membership. The Party had nearly 101.29 million members and more than 5.43 million primary-level organizations at the end of 2025, according to figures released in June by the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee. At its fifth plenary session from Oct 26 to 29, the 20th CPC Central Committee adopted a resolution on major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, setting out measures to address these challenges. In his explanation of the resolution, Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, noted that for more than a century, the CPC had grown stronger by relying on its own efforts and the support of the people to resolve internal problems. Xi also noted that full and rigorous Party self-governance remains a long-term strategic task. While the vast majority of Party members are exemplary, he said problems and hidden dangers remain that could undermine the Party's advanced nature and integrity and jeopardize its long-term governance. The resolution stresses that the Party's long-term governance, the enduring peace China enjoys and the complex circumstances it faces make it all the more important to "be ever ready to protect against potential dangers in time of peace and make our Party more competent and stronger". It identifies strict management of officials as the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance and emphasizes that Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in this endeavor, calling for a well-knit organizational system characterized by cross-level alignment and effective implementation. British economist John Ross, a senior fellow at the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University of China, attributed the CPC's continued vitality to its ability to adapt to China's changing development needs. As China developed from a poor country into a major technological power, the Party had to adjust its policies and leadership rather than rely on approaches suited to earlier stages, he said. Sławomir Majman, deputy director of the Institute of Security and International Development in Poland, highlighted the CPC's ability to translate political decisions into action. Drawing on Poland's experience before 1989, Majman said that the CPC had played an active role in advancing reforms, with its organizational structure helping ensure that decisions were carried out rather than remaining on paper. He also emphasized the importance of combating corruption, comparing its destructive effects on a country's development prospects to those of cancer. Majman described the Chinese leadership's emphasis on fighting corruption as "something very positive and very important". He also said that In the Name of the People, a Chinese drama centered on the fight against corruption, is his favorite Chinese television series. The resolution adopted at the plenary session says that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity or desire to commit corruption is both an important policy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental principle in the fight against corruption. According to official Chinese figures, since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people. They have also investigated and handled 1.644 million cases involving pointless formalities, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, with 2.257 million people criticized, educated or disciplined. Efforts praised Former British lawmaker George Galloway also spoke positively of China's efforts to hold corrupt officials accountable. "I think the general secretary of the Party has made remarkable progress in dealing with corrupt officials," he said. Galloway emphasized the importance of preventing political office from becoming a means of personal enrichment and maintaining a clear distinction between public responsibilities and private financial interests. Ratu Josaia Niudamu, Fiji's assistant minister for justice, said corruption remains a major challenge for smaller countries, particularly when it involves politicians and public officials. "We have learned a lot," he said, expressing hope that China's anti-corruption experience could help Fiji strengthen its policies and laws. For Gulnar Shaimergenova, director of the China Studies Center in Kazakhstan, the significance of sustained Party self-governance extends beyond disciplinary measures to the broader challenge of maintaining effective institutions and public trust. "Party self-governance is not simply a matter of disciplinary campaigns," Shaimergenova said in a written interview with China Daily. "Its long-term significance lies in transforming accountability, supervision and responsible conduct into regular institutional practices." She said this approach was particularly relevant to China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), as translating long-term development priorities into practical outcomes requires consistent policy implementation and sustained accountability. "While domestic governance systems differ, the broader lesson is that institutions must be capable of adapting, correcting mistakes and maintaining consistency between their commitments and their performance," she said. "Public confidence cannot be taken for granted," she added, stressing that it must be reinforced through accountability, effective governance and tangible improvements in people's lives. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: 'Elephant canteen' steers herds away, stems farmer losses
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
Editor's note: As protection of the planet's flora, fauna and resources becomes increasingly important, China Daily is publishing a series of stories to illustrate the country's commitment to safeguarding the natural world. The early morning mist rolling over Nanbanghe village in Pu'er, Yunnan province, used to carry an underlying edge of tension. In this part of Southwest China, wild Asian elephants are not just occasional visitors; they are an indelible part of daily life. The massive animals move fluidly through farmland, dense forests and narrow rural roads, sometimes gathering in impressive herds. Li Meixian, Party chief of the village, recalls times when as many as 40 to 50 elephants appeared in the area at once. Even recently, more than 30 have remained actively roaming the surrounding countryside. On paper, their persistent presence reflects a remarkable triumph of conservation. Yunnan's wild Asian elephant population has grown from 293 in 2018 to nearly 400, according to official figures. Yet for the farming communities sitting directly along these ancient migration corridors, that conservation success brought a harrowing, everyday dilemma: how can people protect their crops, their homes and their personal safety while actively making room for a protected, four-metric-ton species? Pu'er set out to answer that question not with barriers or conflict, but with an integrated package of measures combining managed food source bases, constant monitoring, insurance compensation and financial backing for local rural industries. In Nanbanghe, the most visible and innovative piece of this strategy is known locally as the "elephant canteen".

item.title: Rise of domestic brands reeling in 'China haul'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
Mariana Rizzo, a 23-year-old Italian studying architecture at the University of Naples Federico II, has made shopping part of her experience of everyday life in China. She first visited the country in 2023 and has returned three times, with some trips lasting almost two months. Her shopping list includes beauty products, clothing, accessories, snacks, technology and lifestyle goods, as well as items that are harder to find in Italy. "When it comes to Chinese brands, one of the beauty brands I really like is Flower Knows. I love their makeup, but also the packaging and the attention they put into the design," she said. Rizzo is among the growing number of foreigners visiting the country for the "China haul" — a trend of international travelers filling their suitcases with Chinese products before heading home. Underpinning the phenomenon is the growing appreciation of the quality and modern appeal of Chinese brands often highlighted on social media and shopping platforms. "Sometimes I see something on Xiaohongshu or Douyin and think, 'I need to find this when I go to China!'" Rizzo said. "For me, shopping in China is not just about getting something cheaper. It's about having access to a much wider variety of products and experiencing the trends and lifestyle of the country directly," she said. Her favorite purchases include a qipao, the traditional dress worn by Chinese women, and a DJI Osmo Pocket 4 camera for recording her travels. "Buying it in China was particularly interesting because DJI is a Chinese technology brand, and I was able to discover and buy it directly there," said Rizzo, adding that the camera was considerably cheaper in China than in Italy. She has also noticed growing interest in Chinese products and brands among her friends and classmates in Italy, and sometimes she introduces them to brands she has discovered.

item.title: A new chapter begins: Giant pandas return to Zoo Atlanta
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
Two giant pandas from China, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, made their public debut at Zoo Atlanta on Nov 6, ending a two-year absence of giant pandas from the city. Their arrival opens a new chapter in giant panda conservation, building on 25 years of collaboration between Zoo Atlanta and its Chinese partners. Visitors welcomed the pair, while zoo officials highlighted the role of pandas in promoting wildlife conservation and cultural exchange. (Reporter: May Zhou, Video: Chelsea Ge)

item.title: Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger to win CSL title after 21 yrs
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger to win CSL title after 21 years By Li Yingxue | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-11-08 19:11 Share - WeChat Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger 3-1 at home on Sunday to clinch the 2026 Chinese Super League title on the final day of the season at Suoyuwan Football Stadium in Dalian, Liaoning province. [Photo/Xinhua] Snow blanketed the pitch, while the stands glowed blue. Neither the heavy snowfall nor the pressure of a title decider could stop Dalian Yingbo from making history. Dalian Yingbo beat Tianjin Jinmen Tiger 3-1 at home on Sunday to clinch the 2026 Chinese Super League title on the final day of the season, in front of 62,619 spectators at Suoyuwan Football Stadium in Dalian, Liaoning province. The triumph marks the return of the Chinese top-flight title to Dalian for the first time since 2005, when Dalian Shide last won the championship.
